item.title: 2nd Friday ArtWalk: Extended Museum Hours — Fri Nov 13, 5:00 PM — Ackland Art Museum
item.description:

item.title: NCLAFF. UA Wolf Among Swans — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
Um Lobo Entre os Cisnes (A Wolf Among Swans). 2025. Dir. Marcos Schechtman, Helena Varvaki (Brazil). 112 min. Thiago Soares, one of Brazil's greatest ballet dancers, is offering a compelling study of artistic excellence emerging from marginalized communities. Because the mentor-student relationship invites critical discussion about power dynamics, cultural transmission, and the transformative process of artistic formation. And because its cross-cultural narrative-from Rio's favelas to the Royal Ballet in London-provides rich material for examining class mobility, cultural capital, and the globalization of the performing arts. A Wolf Among Swans is a biographical drama that follows the extraordinary journey of Thiago Soares, a boy from the suburbs of Rio de Janeiro who trades the rhythms of hip hop for the discipline of classical ballet.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.description: 5 Points Gallery is pleased to present Carolina, or Thereabouts, a new exhibition of mixed-media paintings by Featured Artist Jenny Blazing exploring the shifting nature of place through observation, memory, and imagination. Grounded in Blazing’s experiences of Carolina, the layered works draw from travel, accumulated visual memories, and unexpected connections that emerge as the paintings evolve to create landscapes that feel familiar without belonging to any single geography. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our ten Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. Join us for the Opening Reception on Friday, October 16, 2026, from 6–9 pm to meet the artist. Carolina, or Thereabouts runs from October 15 through November 14, 2026. item.description:

item.title: NCLAFF. COMPARSA — Sat Nov 14, 2:00 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
Comparsa. 2025. Dir. Vickie Curtis and Doug Anderson. (Guatemala/USA). 79 min. Comparsa is a compelling, intimate portrait of young women using art to heal their community in the aftermath of violence. From the shadows of a Guatemalan barrio scared into silence, sisters Lesli and Lupe lead a luminous rebellion-unleashing joy, art, and radical truth in an epic fight for survival. The film sheds light on the true cost of gender-based violence, the role of art in building resistance and resilience, and the transformative potential of grassroots youth action.

item.title: Faculty Recital: Gabriel Richard — The Three Bs — Sat Nov 14, 8:00 PM — East Duke 201 - Nelson Music Room
item.description:
Explore three centuries of musical innovation as faculty violinist Gabriel Richard presents "The Three Bs: Bach, Bartók, Boulez-Perspectives on Form from the Baroque to the Contemporary."
The program traces the evolution of musical form through a violin transcription of Bach's BWV 542, Bartók's Sonata for Solo Violin, Boulez's Anthèmes I, and Bach's Partita No. 2 for Solo Violin. Moving from the intricate architecture of the Baroque to the bold musical languages of the 20th century, the recital reveals striking connections among three composers whose works continually challenge and redefine the possibilities of sound.
This event is free and open to the public. All are welcome.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.description:
The North Carolina Jewish Studies Seminar welcomes Federica Francesconi, Associate Professor of History and Director of the Judaic Studies Program at the University at Albany, SUNY. Her research and publications address the social, religious, and cultural aspects of the early modern history of Jews in Italy, focusing on the multifaceted politics and dynamics of ghetto life. She has held fellowships in Europe, Israel, and the United States. She served as Viterbi Visiting Professor in Mediterranean Jewish Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, and has been a fellow at the Herbert D. Katz Center for Advanced Judaic Studies at the University of Pennsylvania and the Oxford Centre for Hebrew and Jewish Studies.

item.title: Opera FM — Sun Nov 15, 3:30 PM — Carolina Theatre of Durham
item.description:
Experience opera’s golden age. A live orchestra, a theatrical radio host, and all the drama. From the elegant streets of Spain to the bustling boulevards of Paris and the grand opera houses of Italy, Opera FM brings together some of the most unforgettable characters ever set to music. Tune in to opera’s biggest emotions, inspired by the golden age of vintage radio. You’ll hear the sparkle and sophistication of Rossini’s beloved barber, the youthful charm of Donizetti’s regiment, the bittersweet yearnings of Puccini and Weill, and the fiery passions of Verdi’s immortal heroes. Don’t touch that dial, now.

item.title: NCLAFF. GAMA RAYS — Sun Nov 15, 5:30 PM — Richard White Lecture Hall
item.description:
GAMA RAYS & CHATINOS HOY Y SIEMPRE 5:30 PM. Serenade with MARIACHI TORO 6:00 pm - 7:00 pm | Indigenous South America, Mexico, and the U.S. *Ticketed event (REQUEST TICKETS TO: mlr34@duke.edu, las@duke.edu)
Gama Rays. Dir. J.J. Ortiz, Gia Jiménez Huamán. 2026. Colombia. 15 min. Kagaba, with English subtitles. The softer voice of Saga María, a female Indigenous philosopher, shares the embodied knowledge and practice of transforming natural fibers into Kogi archives. A rare moment with one of the most traditional Indigenous peoples of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, and probably the most sustainable people on earth.
For the Indigenous Peoples of the Sierra Nevada de Gonawindúa, known in Spanish as the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in the north of Colombia, weaving the traditional mochila (GAMA/backpack) represents the act of creating the world, of recreating life; as such, this is the work of the Indigenous women.
This short is produced by P'alante Producciones, DukeEngage Colombia

Hear her thoughts on how 20th-century sound technologies and mass media shaped American poetic voice.
Book Description:
American Poetic Voice in the Era of Global Broadcast situates American poetry within global media to reveal the broad institutional, technological, and cultural resonances of poetic voice. Reading works by Marianne Moore, W.H. Auden, Frank O'Hara, Adrienne Rich, and Audre Lorde, it traces how poetry intersects with specific sound technologies like the phonograph, telephone, radio, and tape recorder, and various vocal practices and institutions, including elocution instruction, poetry reading circuits, and radio-based cultural diplomacy.

item.title: CEE Seminar - Bacterial biofilms, pigments and javelins — Mon Nov 16, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: Bacteria often grow in biofilms, cell clusters held together by a self-produced matrix. This lifestyle promotes physiological differentiation, making it difficult to control bacterial growth. My group studies the multicellular physiology of Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a metabolically versatile bacterium that produces diverse virulence factors and is a major cause of biofilm-based infections. To visualize and investigate mechanisms underpinning differentiation in biofilms, we use fluorescent reporters and deuterium labeling paired with microscopy of thin sections and live samples. We have shown that biofilm subpopulations employ distinct strategies, such as using oxygen-scavenging complexes and endogenous electron-shuttling compounds called phenazines, to sustain metabolic activity. We also observed that such metabolic differentiation correlates with increased drug tolerance. item.title: Genome Dynamics in the Fungal Kingdom — Mon Nov 16, 12:00 PM — None
item.description:
The lab of Daniel Croll wants to understand how pathogens evolve to cause disease. For this, we focus mainly on major crop pathogens and investigate mechanisms of rapid adaptation. We are interested in how host resistance mechanisms are circumvented, how pesticides become ineffective, and how pathogens are able to cope with climate challenges. We take a broad view in our work and have strong interests in processes of genome evolution at all levels, from transposable element dynamics to broad species comparisons. We combine computational work with empirical analyses from the field to the bench.

item.title: Anna Murray Douglass and a Family of Revolutionaries: A Conversation Reclaiming the Woman at the Center of the Struggle — Mon Nov 16, 2:00 PM — Rubenstein Library Holsti-Anderson Family Assembly Room 153
item.description:
Anna Murray Douglass was a freedom-fighter, strategist, and revolutionary whose contributions have too often been overshadowed by those of her husband, Frederick Douglass. Join author Celeste-Marie Bernier with director, writer, producer, and Duke alumnus Charles Randolph-Wright ("American Prophet: Frederick Douglass in His Own Words"), and Douglass family member Kenneth B. Morris, Jr., for a conversation about "Anna Murray Douglass: Biography of a Revolutionary" (Duke University Press, 2026) the first standalone biography devoted to her life and work.
Drawing on more than thirty years of archival research and collaboration with family descendants, Bernier reveals Anna Murray Douglass's leadership in the struggle against slavery, racism, and white supremacy-from helping secure Frederick Douglass's self-liberation to making the family's homes centers of Underground Railroad activity. item.description:
Raleigh AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup Join us on Dec 8 for the “How to Let Long-tail Guide Your 3D Annotation” workshop with [Eric Hofesmann](https://www.linkedin.com/in/eric-hofesmann/).
**Date, Time and Location**
Dec 08, 2026 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/how-to-let-long-tail-guide-your-3d-annotation-december-8-2026)**
Autonomous driving models rarely fail on the common case. They fail on the long-tail: the pedestrian stepping out from behind a parked truck or a construction zone that matches nothing in the training set. Each of those moments lives in synchronized multi-sensor data, made up of a LiDAR sweep, a ring of cameras, a timestamp, and a calibration. Fixing one means finding it, labeling it in 3D, and proving the next model handles it.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

We are here to protect our democracy. We are standing up for what we believe in. We want to inspire people to join us and grow our movement!Please bring positive signs opposing the OligarchyPlease no mocking signs, no swastikasWe are excited to see you there and stand together for our country!See you every Thursday from 4:30-5:30 engaging drivers in Durham!Please join our Substack: https://substack.com/@engageddefendersfordemocracy?utm_source=global-searchFor more ED4D Mobilize Events: https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/event/ https://www.mobilize.us/engagedefendersfordemocracy/event/842805/
Source: Durham Resistance (In Person)
